get_next_location:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Reads num_of_people input lines containing a current location and a direction, computes each person's next coordinate, and returns the coordinate that occurs most frequently, using the lexicographically smallest coordinate to break ties." get_next_location]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> num_of_people </REF>: int "Number of people/input lines to process."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: list[int] "The most frequent [x, y] coordinate; if multiple coordinates tie, the lexicographically smallest [x, y] coordinate is returned."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize coordinates_list to an empty list. RESULT coordinates_list]
            [COMMAND Initialize people_count to 1. RESULT people_count]
            [COMMAND While people_count is less than or equal to num_of_people, read a line from standard input, split it into tokens, parse x, y, and dir from the first three tokens, apply the four independent direction checks (N: y += 1, S: y -= 1, E: x += 1, W: x -= 1), append [x, y] to coordinates_list, and increment people_count by 1. RESULT coordinates_list]
            [COMMAND Initialize next_dest to an empty list. RESULT next_dest]
            [COMMAND Initialize next_dest_count to an empty list. RESULT next_dest_count]
            [COMMAND For each coordinates in coordinates_list, initialize found to 0 and dest_idx to 0; for each dest in next_dest, if coordinates equals dest, increment next_dest_count[dest_idx], set found to 1, and break; otherwise increment dest_idx; after the inner loop, if found is 0, append coordinates to next_dest and append 1 to next_dest_count. RESULT next_dest]
            [COMMAND Set popular_next_dest to a list containing next_dest[0], set highest_count to next_dest_count[0], and set dest_count_idx to 0. RESULT popular_next_dest]
            [COMMAND For each dest_count in next_dest_count, if dest_count_idx is 0, increment dest_count_idx and continue; if dest_count equals highest_count, append next_dest[dest_count_idx] to popular_next_dest; if dest_count is greater than highest_count, reset popular_next_dest to an empty list, set highest_count to dest_count, and append next_dest[dest_count_idx] to popular_next_dest; increment dest_count_idx at the end of the iteration. RESULT popular_next_dest]
            [COMMAND Check whether len(popular_next_dest) equals 1. RESULT popular_next_dest]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: len(popular_next_dest) == 1]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return popular_next_dest[0]. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: len(popular_next_dest) > 1]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize smallest_number to popular_next_dest[0] and dest_idx to 0. RESULT smallest_number]
            [COMMAND For each dest in popular_next_dest, if dest_idx is 0, increment dest_idx and continue; otherwise, if dest is less than smallest_number, set smallest_number to dest; increment dest_idx at the end of the iteration. RESULT smallest_number]
            [COMMAND Return smallest_number. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
